generation.explanation: The tangent function is defined as tan(x) = sin(x)/cos(x), so it is undefined wherever cos(x) = 0 — at x = ±π/2 and ±3π/2 within [−2π, 2π]. At these x-values the graph has vertical asymptotes: as x approaches one of them, sin(x) is near ±1 while cos(x) shrinks toward 0, so the quotient explodes toward +∞ or −∞ (the sign depends on the side you approach from, since cos changes sign there). That is why the graph splits into separate S-shaped branches between consecutive asymptotes. Use the slider to move x toward an asymptote and watch cos(x) → 0 while tan(x) blows up.
